questions.answer: Home tab → Cells group (Format → Protect Sheet); also the Review tab → Changes group

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What is Merge Cells in Excel?
questions.answer: Merge Cells joins two or more selected adjacent cells into one larger cell. With Merge & Center the contents are also centred, which is useful for a heading spread over several columns.

or.q: Why do we use Merge Cells?
or.answer: We merge cells to make a title or heading span several columns or rows, to give the worksheet a neat, organised look and to make it easier to read.

questions.q: What are the different tabs available in the Format Cells dialog box?
questions.answer: Number (data type such as number, currency, date), Alignment (position and orientation of text), Font (face, size, style, effects), Border (cell borders), Fill/Patterns (background colour) and Protection (locking and hiding cells).

questions.q: Write the steps to AutoFit rows (or columns) in a spreadsheet.
questions.answer: (1) Select the row (or column), or a cell in it. (2) Home tab → Format in the Cells group. (3) Click AutoFit Row Height (or AutoFit Column Width). Or double-click the bottom edge of the row header (right edge of the column header).

questions.q: What is Format Painter? When is it useful in Excel?
questions.answer: Format Painter copies the formatting (font, number format, border, colour) of one cell and applies it to other cells. It is useful when many cells must look the same, saving the effort of formatting each one; double-click to apply it to many ranges.

questions.q: Differentiate between Format Painter and AutoFormat in worksheets.
questions.answer: Format Painter copies the format of a selected cell to other cells chosen by you. AutoFormat (Format as Table) applies a complete predefined table style — fonts, borders, shading, number formats — to a whole range at once.

questions.q: How do you hide and unhide a worksheet?
questions.answer: Hide: right-click the sheet tab and choose Hide. Unhide: right-click any visible sheet tab, choose Unhide, select the hidden sheet from the list and click OK.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Write the steps to protect a worksheet using a password. How do you unprotect it?
questions.answer: Protect: (1) Home tab → Format (Cells group). (2) Choose Protect Sheet. (3) Type a password and click OK. (4) Re-enter the same password to confirm. Now any change shows a warning. Unprotect: Home → Format → Unprotect Sheet → type the same password → OK.

questions.q: Explain the different preset cell styles available in Excel.
questions.answer: (1) Comma — adds commas and two decimal places. (2) Comma [0] — comma style rounded to a whole number. (3) Currency — currency symbol, commas and two decimals. (4) Currency [0] — currency rounded to a whole number. (5) Percent — changes the number to a percentage with a % sign. (6) Normal — returns to the general format. Other styles include Heading 1, Good, Bad and Neutral.

questions.q: How do you hide and unhide a column in Excel?
questions.answer: Hide: (1) Click the column header to select it. (2) Right-click and choose Hide; the column disappears but its data remains. Unhide: (1) Select the columns on both sides of the hidden column. (2) Right-click and choose Unhide; the column becomes visible again. Rows are hidden and unhidden the same way.

sections.title: Long answer question. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the three places where formatting tools are available in Excel 2007, and the tabs of the Format Cells dialog box.
questions.answer: (1) Home tab — Font, Alignment and Number groups for the most common formatting. (2) Mini toolbar — appears on right-clicking a cell: font, size, bold, italic, colours, borders, Merge & Center, number styles, Format Painter. (3) Format Cells dialog box — opened with Ctrl+1, the dialog launcher or right-click → Format Cells. Its tabs: Number (General, Number, Currency, Date, Time, Percentage), Alignment (position, orientation, wrap, merge), Font, Border, Fill/Patterns and Protection.

or.q: How do you apply AutoFormat (Format as Table) and cell styles to a worksheet?
or.answer: Format as Table: (1) Select the cells. (2) Home → Styles → Format as Table. (3) Choose a style from Light, Medium or Dark. (4) Tick 'My table has headers' and click OK; change the style from Table Tools → Design. Cell styles: (1) Select the cells. (2) Home → Styles → Cell Styles. (3) Choose a style such as Heading 1, Comma, Currency or Percent. (4) Right-click a style → Delete to remove it.
